I had one of the worst shopping experiences with Zepto.

I ordered a mouse and keyboard combo with Open Box Delivery. During delivery, the delivery executive only showed me the keyboard and mouse and asked for the OTP. After I provided the OTP and properly opened the mouse packaging, I discovered that the USB receiver (dongle) was missing, making the wireless mouse completely unusable.

This is extremely disappointing because Open Box Delivery is meant to verify that the correct product has been delivered—not to inspect every internal component or accessory sealed inside the packaging.

Customers should not be penalized for missing items that cannot reasonably be verified during doorstep delivery. Instead of taking responsibility, Zepto has chosen to hide behind its policy and leave the customer with a defective, unusable product.

I expected much better service from Zepto. If this is how genuine issues are handled, I cannot recommend ordering electronics from them. Think twice before purchasing anything through Zepto, especially products with Open Box Delivery.

text:
Avoid Zepto. This was one of the worst customer support experiences I've had.

I ordered 3 Amul Red Tetra Pack milk cartons, but instead received 6 Amul Moti milk pouches. These are different products with different packaging, and the quantity delivered did not match my order. The product I ordered was also more expensive than what I received.

If the ordered product was unavailable, the correct approach would have been to inform me, seek my approval for a substitute, or issue a refund. Instead, the product was changed without my knowledge or consent.

I immediately contacted support, attaching screenshots of my order showing the Amul Red Tetra Pack and photographs of the Amul Moti milk pouches that were actually delivered. Despite this clear evidence, I received a generic response claiming that the seller had "thoroughly reviewed" the order and confirmed that the delivered product matched the order and app description, so no refund or exchange would be provided.

I then pointed out the obvious facts:

Amul Red Tetra Pack and Amul Moti milk pouches are completely different products.
The delivered quantity did not match my order.
I asked how they concluded that the order was fulfilled correctly despite the evidence.
Instead of answering these questions, they simply claimed they had tried calling me twice. I never received any missed call or answered call on my registered number. I even asked them to provide the date, time, and phone number from which they supposedly called, but they ignored that request as well.
I also requested the evidence used during their so-called verification, such as packing verification records or CCTV footage from the packing station, if available. Again, no response—just the same copied-and-pasted template stating that the seller had verified everything and no refund or exchange would be processed.

Since Zepto provides virtually no effective customer support and directs customers to email, I contacted the delivery partner myself. I have an audio recording in which he stated that the seller had intentionally substituted the product and that if the customer complained, they would normally accept a return or process a refund.

I later spoke directly with the seller, and I have that conversation recorded as well. The seller admitted that the originally scanned tetra packs were damaged and were replaced with six milk pouches before dispatch. Even more importantly, the seller confirmed that no one from Zepto had contacted them regarding my complaint before my claim was rejected.

This directly contradicts Zepto's repeated claim that the seller had thoroughly reviewed the order. Either no proper investigation was conducted, or the responses sent to me were simply generic templates without verifying the facts.

I informed Zepto of this new information and even shared the recordings, requesting a proper re-investigation. Their response? The exact same copied message yet again:

"The seller has thoroughly reviewed your order and confirmed that the product was delivered in good condition as per the app description. Unfortunately, the seller is unable to process a refund or exchange."
I even emailed their main support address with the entire conversation, hoping it might reach a real support team rather than an automated system. I received no response, even after waiting until the next day. The in-app chat simply kept directing me to email support, and there appears to be no customer care phone number available for customers to escalate genuine issues.

I am a regular buyer of Amul Red Tetra milk, and my order history clearly reflects that. I have never ordered Amul Moti milk pouches. It makes no sense for a customer to purchase a more expensive product and then falsely claim they received a cheaper substitute.

The most disappointing part wasn't the delivery mistake—it was Zepto's refusal to investigate despite screenshots, photographs, audio recordings, and even the seller's own admission. Every response was a copy-paste template that ignored the actual facts.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend ordering from Zepto. If something goes wrong with your order, don't expect a meaningful investigation or accessible customer support.

text:
I am extremely disappointed with my recent experience with Swiggy. I ordered fried rice through the Swiggy app, expecting food that was safe and fit to eat. Unfortunately, what was delivered was of shockingly poor quality. The rice was not properly cooked—it was raw, hard, and clearly undercooked. This wasn’t just a matter of taste or preference; it was food that should never have been served to a customer.

What makes this even more concerning is that this order was meant for children. Serving undercooked food could easily lead to stomach issues or foodborne illness. Had my children consumed it, it could have caused serious health problems. This is not something that should ever be taken lightly.

When I contacted Swiggy support, I expected them to take responsibility and provide a refund. Instead, I was told to leave a review for the restaurant so they could improve their quality in the future. However, when I requested a refund for receiving unsafe and inedible food, I was simply told that no refund could be processed.

This response is completely unacceptable. I placed my order through Swiggy, not directly with the restaurant. As the platform that accepts my payment and chooses to partner with these restaurants, Swiggy has a responsibility to ensure that its customers receive food that meets basic quality and safety standards. Passing the responsibility entirely to the restaurant and asking customers to “leave a review” is not a solution.

The biggest question is: Who takes accountability? If someone had fallen sick after consuming this food—especially children—would Swiggy still say that leaving a review is the only option? Customer safety should always come before company policies.

I have always trusted Swiggy for convenience and reliability, but this experience has severely damaged that trust. It is disappointing to see that customer concerns about food safety are handled with such little seriousness.

I sincerely hope Swiggy reviews its customer support policies, takes greater responsibility for the quality of food delivered through its platform, and ensures that customers are treated fairly when they receive food that is clearly unsafe to consume. This experience has left me feeling extremely let down, both by the restaurant and by Swiggy’s unwillingness to stand behind the service it provides.

I have been using Swiggy for years, but this was one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had.

I ordered McDonald’s worth ₹177. The delivery was delayed, and I noticed the delivery partner went in the opposite direction to another society before coming to me. I immediately contacted Swiggy support, expecting a replacement or a full refund since the order was unusable. Instead, they offered me just ₹30—approximately one-sixth of what I paid.

When I explained that the food was completely spoiled and couldn’t even be eaten, support simply kept repeating that this was the “best resolution as per company policy.” Apparently, according to Swiggy, delivering food that is entirely ruined is worth only a ₹30 refund.

The most disappointing part wasn’t even the damaged food—it was the complete lack of accountability. There was no genuine effort to understand the issue or make things right, only scripted responses and policy excuses.

If this is how Swiggy treats customers when an order is completely ruined, it raises serious concerns about how much they value customer satisfaction.

After this experience, I’ll think twice before ordering through Swiggy again and cannot recommend it to anyone expecting reliable service or fair customer support.

On top of that, customers are expected to pay delivery charges, platform fees, handling charges, and other additional costs, making every order far more expensive than it should be.

Despite paying these extra charges, quick service is often lacking. Delayed deliveries, poor customer support, and difficulty resolving genuine issues have made the overall experience frustrating.

One of my biggest concerns is the impact these platforms have on restaurants. Many restaurant owners have shared that the commissions charged by food delivery platforms are so high that they have no choice but to increase menu prices to remain profitable. Ultimately, customers end up paying more while restaurants earn less.

Another concern repeatedly raised by restaurant owners is around advertisements and discount campaigns. Several owners have said they feel pressured to participate in paid ads and promotional discounts because they believe declining these programs results in reduced visibility and fewer orders. According to these owners, restaurants often bear the full cost of discounts while also paying substantial commissions and advertising fees. If these experiences are widespread, it creates an unhealthy environment where businesses feel compelled to spend more simply to remain competitive.

Restaurants should be free to decide whether they want to run promotions without fearing a significant drop in discoverability or orders. A fair marketplace should reward quality, customer satisfaction, and service—not just advertising spend.

The lack of transparency in commissions, pricing, and promotional costs is another issue that deserves attention. Customers often don’t realize why menu prices are inflated, and many assume restaurants are overcharging, when in reality the pricing may be influenced by platform-related costs.

Healthy competition is essential. When a few large platforms dominate the market, both customers and restaurants can end up with fewer choices, higher prices, and reduced bargaining power. I hope the industry moves toward a more transparent and balanced ecosystem where restaurants are treated fairly, customers receive better value, and success depends on quality rather than paid visibility.

text:
I had a terrible experience with Swiggy's cancellation policy. I accidentally placed an order due to auto-payment and cancelled it within seconds.At the time of cancellation.

The restaurant had not started preparing the food.
No delivery partner was assigned.
The order had not been picked up or dispatched.

Despite this, Swiggy charged me a 100% cancellation fee of ₹777and refunded ₹0.

I understand if there are small administrative or convenience charges, but charging the entire order value without providing any service is completely unfair. There should be a 30–60 second cancellation grace period for accidental orders. Instead, Swiggy penalizes genuine customers even when no actual cost has been incurred.

This policy feels one-sided and erodes customer trust. I hope Swiggy revises its cancellation policy to be fair and transparent. Until then, customers should be aware that even an instant cancellation can result in losing the full amount.
